newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Ex-colonial adviser pledges support for HK's Tung.
newsitem.headline: Ex-colonial adviser pledges support for HK's Tung.

text.p: One of Britain's most trusted advisers in Hong Kong, now chosen to lead future chief executive Tung Chee-hwa's cabinet, pledged on Sunday to work for a smooth transition to Chinese sovereignty.
Tung on Friday named Sir S.Y. Chung, a veteran adviser to three colonial governors, as convenor of his 15-strong future inner cabinet of advisers, the Executive Council.
"I am very appeciative of...Mr Tung Chee-hwa, in asking me to come out of retirement...to serve again," Chung, 79, said in a statement received on Sunday.
Chung, who will serve for two years as convenor, angered Beijing in the early 1980s for expressing a lack of confidence in Hong Kong's future but was later forgiven.
His name was bandied around for a while in the early 1990s as a potential candidate for the territory's first chief executive after it was returned to Chinese rule.
Tung also appointed to his cabinet two members of Governor Chris Patten's cabinet, housing authority chief Rosanna Wong and businessman Raymond Ch'ien.
Former Hong Kong chief justice Ti Liang Yang, who competed with Tung for the chief executive post, also was selected.

Noticeably absent, though not unexpectedly, were members of Hong Kong's pro-democracy parties, frequent critics of Beijing in the run-up to the territory's handover on June 30 after more than 150 years of British rule.
